card.title: The Leak Is Spreading
card.instruction: Interpret every new question or coincidence as evidence that concealed information is escaping faster than it can be contained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why are there three copies of our private resignation letter on your desk?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One for each of us and a spare. Nobody else has seen it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The spare is a conversation waiting to happen. Shred it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I use the accounts shredder? Ours is jammed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accounts already? We haven't destroyed one copy and it's reached another department. Who there knows?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sees extra copies as exposure, A3 treats the spare as future disclosure, and A5 interprets borrowing a shredder as information reaching accounts.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's spare-copy explanation makes A3 order destruction; B4's jammed-shredder workaround causes A5's departmental-spread alarm.

relationship.evidence: B2 accounts for all copies and B4 asks for a practical way to carry out shredding.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's destruction solution to infer that containment has already enlarged the audience.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies a private joint resignation letter and B2 the two personal copies plus spare.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's not-destroyed-one-yet comparison follows B4's blocked shredder and proposed other department.
